items.title: George Shearing interviewed by Joe Williams, New York City, New York, March 8, 1996
items.q: Dizzy Gillespie and the fellas kind of upset up.

ctx.x: That’s right. There’s this wonderful story about an Indian who came over here and played jazz over here and he went back home you know. And they said, “You know you’ve been in America too long. Why don’t you make it simple? You know put the sock cymbal on two, seven, eleven and thirteen.”
I love it. Two, eleven — Oh my God. That’s beautiful. It did get a little out there. Dizzy Gillespie and the fellas kind of upset up.

Oh he was very authentic. Dizzy. Well Chano Pozo, you know, and that’s where McKibbon learned all that stuff, from Chano Pozo. And then of course McKibbon came with me, and Tjader, Cal Tjader. And then Armando.
